title: I Posted the Longarm-Quilt Hours After They Camped My Frame

parts.text: I stepped into frame one at 11:02 a.m. and chair Lila was already using my numbered leaders. The board said: FOUR HOURS. ONE FRAME. BASTING STAYS WITH THE BOOKING. I was thirty-three, guild secretary, holding a calendar that listed our quilt. Lila shrugged. "Chairs keep the frame." I photographed the board, the booking, and her batting on my leaders. Then I asked for the frame hours. At 11:10 the guild desk pinged why Lila's batting was on our leaders. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The guild desk can see Lila's batting on frame one during our four hours.

social.video_title: She camped my numbered quilt frame — Part 1/2
social.description: Longarm studio, a chair on my leaders, a four-hour clock she posted. I logged the batting. Would you have asked for the frame hours?

parts.text: Lila called it basting until the desk asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the frame still. The leaders went back to my numbered clamps. Lila ran a slot of their own and told the next chair atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word people use when a booking exists. Policy now has a second line: CHAIRS DO NOT KEEP THE FRAME. I keep our hours on a labeled card. Lila brown-bags her batting. The frame finally looks like a booking, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Chairs do not keep the frame — Part 2/2
social.description: Frame hours, numbered leaders, and a second line on the board. Was basting ever our four hours?
